currency.source: @fawazahmed0/currency-api: CC0, republished daily on npm, no key. US dollar to every currency; jsDelivr first, its Cloudflare mirror second.

gemini.source: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (paid tier; page updated 2026-10-19). The free tier is free of charge.

analysis.source: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing as republished by getmaxim.ai and anotherwrapper.com (Google's data of 2026-09), read 2026-10-22. Thinking bills as text out. The free tier is free of charge.
analysis.estimateSource: A typical 3-minute call: about 1,000 transcript tokens plus 500 of instructions in; summary, fields and memory note out.

TELNYX.source: telnyx.com/pricing/call-control (Voice API 0.002, media streaming 0.0035, recording 0.002) + telnyx.com/pricing/elastic-sip (US local in from 0.0032, out from 0.005). Telnyx publishes no India rates (/pricing/elastic-sip/in and /pricing/call-control/in list none, checked 2026-10-22): calls to India show without Telnyx's charge.

TWILIO.source: twilio.com/en-us/voice/pricing/us ('current as of August 2026': local in 0.0085, out 0.014, Media Streams 0.0044) + /pricing/in (checked 2026-10-22: to Indian mobiles 0.0496, landlines 0.0699; OUTBOUND_IN is the mobile rate, most leads are mobiles); recording 0.0025.

providersWithoutRates.VOICELINK: No published rate: each account's plan sets its own inbound_rate, outbound_rate and pulse_seconds (app.voicelink.co.in/documentation/plans and the API context file, read 2026-10-21). The engine takes each call's own charge from GET /api/v1/call-log/details (total_cost, rupees) instead.

pipeline.note: What the engine bills each part of a PIPELINE stack on (costs.pipeline_cost), by model. stt: the whole call's minutes (the stream is open from start to end); llm: tokens in and out (thinking counts as out); tts: characters sent, or minutes of audio made for the token-billed ones (Gemini about 1,500 audio tokens a minute, 25 a second).

nova-3.source: deepgram.com/pricing: Nova-3 Multilingual streaming, pay as you go.

sonic-3.6.source: cartesia.ai/pricing: 1 credit = 1 character, Startup plan $49 for 1.25M credits.

gpt-4o-mini-tts.source: developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing: $12 per 1M audio tokens out, about $0.015 a minute.

gemini-3.8-flash-tts.source: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (updated 2026-10-22): $9 per 1M audio tokens out ($18 from 2027-01-01); text in $0.50/M, left out.

gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts.source: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (updated 2026-10-22): $6 per 1M audio tokens out ($12 from 2027-01-01); text in $0.50/M, left out.

estimate.source: backend/voice/research/gemini-cost-2026-10-17.md: with session rotation, a booking agent (about 1,200 prompt tokens a turn, engine sections included) costs $0.0348 a talk-minute and a 5,479-token prompt $0.079.

tools.source: backend/voice/tools.py: the booking functions' declarations plus their '# Your tools' lines are about 2,100 characters; a custom tool sends its description twice (declaration and prompt) plus its parameters. A use reads the tool's answer as text and keeps the line open while it runs.

stack.note: What each stack part costs per minute of call, from the vendors' list prices, read 2026-10-22. Derived ones say how. Settings and the voice picker show these; the engine's own costs.py bills realtime Gemini from its tokens.
